Make the ChatGPT<->Claude Code bridge actually live, over GitHub Issues

The relay was blocked on a deployed HTTP host that does not exist. That was
treated as "no live bridge is possible." It wasn't: the mission's own Wave 5
listed a GitHub-mediated task packet as an available path, and GitHub is
already a durable, authenticated, always-on store both ends can reach with no
new host and no new spend.

src/github-relay.mjs implements that transport, and it has now carried a real
task end to end on real infrastructure (issue #30):

  producer opens issue #30 (label agent-relay:task, fenced uberbond-task packet)
    -> worker polls, claims under a 1800s lease (comment 5348571058)
    -> worker runs real bounded work: npm run test:deterministic
       => 1092 tests, 1050 pass, 0 fail, 42 skipped, exit 0
    -> worker posts a uberbond-result receipt (comment 5348593358)
    -> issue labelled agent-relay:done and closed

No mock at any hop. Real issue, real comment ids, real timestamps, real
measured numbers.

A REAL DEFECT THE LIVE RUN FOUND, that no fixture could:
issue bodies come back HTML-escaped through some GitHub clients (`"` as
`"`), so JSON.parse failed and the relay reported zero claimable tasks
while a valid task sat open -- a silent, total failure of the bridge. Worse,
the escaping is inconsistent between endpoints on the same client: the issue
body was escaped, its comments were not. extractFencedJson now tries raw and
falls back to single-pass entity decoding (single-pass so a literal
"&#34;" is never double-decoded into a quote), with regression tests for
both directions.

Same contract, different wire -- not a second relay: this module imports
ZERO_EFFECTS, hasSecret(), and validResult() from cloud-agent-relay.mjs and
compiles packets with the same compileAgentTask(), so the two transports
cannot drift on what they consider safe. A result claiming any nonzero
external effect is rejected identically on both.

Also staged for unattended, device-off operation:
- scripts/github-relay-worker.mjs -- runs ONLY three allowlisted npm scripts
  and reports UNSUPPORTED_OBJECTIVE otherwise; it never executes free text
  from an issue body, because "anyone who can open an issue" must not mean
  "anyone who can run code in CI".
- .github/workflows/agent-relay-worker.yml -- fires on issues opened/labeled
  plus an hourly cron, concurrency-guarded, permissions limited to
  issues:write + contents:read.

Status is honestly LIVE_UNPROVEN, not VERIFIED_LIVE: the one live run was
driven by an interactive session acting as the worker. The unattended path has
never executed because GitHub Actions on this account is failing at the
infrastructure level -- CI ran clean through 2026-07-17, then every run from
fe51c3c onward dies in ~3-10s with 404 job logs, which dates it to an Actions
billing/quota lapse rather than the code.

Honest limitation recorded in the module, the capability graph, and the docs:
GitHub labels and comments are not database row locks. resolveLease() resolves
a race deterministically after the fact (earliest server-assigned comment id
wins, same answer regardless of asker or comment order) but cannot prevent
duplicated work that already happened. Fine for a few owner-initiated tasks
and one worker; not for high concurrency. cloud-agent-relay.mjs, with real
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED proven against a real PostgreSQL server,
stays the transport to promote once a real host exists.

Audit and harden the governed ChatGPT<->Claude cloud relay (PR #28)

Real, verified defect fixes and gap closures found while auditing the
merged relay (src/cloud-agent-relay.mjs, server.mjs /api/agent-relay/*,
scripts/uberbond-mcp.mjs relay tools) against the mission's Wave 2-4
requirements -- each proven, not asserted:

- Fixed a double-escaped SECRET_VALUE regex (`Bearer\\s+\\S+` inside a
  regex literal matches a literal backslash, never real whitespace) that
  let a raw "Bearer <token>" string past the secret scanner when nested
  under a non-secret-shaped key.
- Fixed an unanchored `sk-`/`ghp_` pattern that false-positived on ordinary
  ids -- found live via the new end-to-end proof, which rejected a normal
  taskId ("e2e-task-1787174626471") because it contains "sk-1787..." as a
  mid-word substring. Anchored both patterns with \b.
- Added the rate limiting the mission's Wave 3 requires (previously
  entirely absent): a sliding one-minute-per-IP limiter on all
  /api/agent-relay/* routes, config.agentRelay.rateLimitPerMinute.
- Added the heartbeat lease-extension the mission's Wave 3/8 require
  (previously entirely absent -- only claim/submit existed): a real
  heartbeatCloudRelayTask() reusing store.heartbeatJob()'s existing
  ownership enforcement, POST /api/agent-relay/tasks/:taskId/heartbeat,
  and the uberbond_relay_heartbeat MCP tool. Without this, any relay task
  running longer than the 5-minute lock timeout risked stale-lease
  reclaim mid-task.
- Added relayHealthSummary() (queued/active/completed/dead-letter counts,
  oldest queued task, stale-lease count) wired into GET
  /api/agent-relay/health, closing the mission's Wave 9 observability gap
  without exposing any task payload.

Real proof obtained this wave (not fake-store-only):
- A real local HTTP server (server.mjs) and a real local MCP process
  (scripts/uberbond-mcp.mjs) driven over actual stdio JSON-RPC, wired
  together over real localhost HTTP: init -> tool list -> poll -> claim ->
  heartbeat -> submit -> rejected replay, with every byte of captured
  process stdout/stderr scanned and confirmed to never contain the raw
  relay token.
- Real embedded PostgreSQL 18 concurrency proof: claimJobsByType's
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED under two workers racing for one relay task,
  excludeTypes protecting relay jobs from normal workers, and
  target-agent isolation (22/22 in tests/postgres-store-live.test.mjs).
